subtype: Approach: feeling ready because the page looks familiar [Pitfall]
passage: I'm Jiya, and I closed my science book with a big smile. Photosynthesis, I had it. I had read the page four times and the picture of the leaf was in my head. At dinner Mummy put down her spoon and asked, "Beti, tell me how a plant makes its food." I opened my mouth. Sun. Leaf. Green. Then nothing came. "It takes light," I said, and stopped. My brother Arnab giggled. I felt my ears go hot. I had thought it was in my head. It was only that the page looked familiar. After dinner I opened the book again and tried to write the steps.

qa.q: What did Jiya's mother ask at dinner?
qa.a: She asked how a plant makes its food.

qa.q: What did Jiya feel when she could not explain the steps at dinner?
qa.a: She felt embarrassed and surprised, since her ears went hot. She had believed she knew it.

qa.q: What could Jiya do differently to check her learning before dinner next time, and why?
qa.a: She could close the book and say the steps aloud to herself or a toy. She would find the gaps before anybody else asks.

qa.q: How might Arnab see Jiya's answer at dinner?
qa.a: Arnab finds it funny to see his sister go quiet, which is why he giggles. He may not realise it stung her.

grounding: A girl closes the book thinking she knows photosynthesis, but when her mother asks her to explain she cannot say the steps.

subtype: Approach: feeling ready because the page looks familiar [Pitfall]
passage: Note to Ma'am, in Ganga's school diary: Ganga told me on Tuesday evening that she was ready for Wednesday's science test. She had read the photosynthesis pages and said they all 'looked familiar'. I asked her to explain it to me with the book shut. She said, 'Leaves make food... with the sun... and something.' She couldn't tell me what goes in or what comes out. She was upset and stayed up late re-reading. I'm writing so you know she did try, and that we will practise explaining out loud before the next test. Aditi (Ganga's mother)

qa.q: What did Ganga say the pages looked like?
What was Ganga feeling when she couldn't explain what goes in or comes out?
qa.a: She was upset, realising that recognising the pages wasn't the same as knowing the steps.

qa.q: What should Ganga try before the next test?
qa.a: Explain the topic aloud with the book shut, as her mother plans, and re-read only the parts she can't explain.

qa.q: How does Aditi see what happened?
qa.a: Aditi wants the teacher to know Ganga tried hard, and sees explaining out loud as the fix for next time.

grounding: Shows a girl who thinks she knows photosynthesis because the pages look familiar, but cannot explain the steps when her mother asks.

subtype: Approach: feeling ready because the page looks familiar [Pitfall]
passage:
Sunday night
Science test tomorrow. I read photosynthesis this afternoon, twice, and closed the book feeling great. I could see the whole page in my head: the green leaf picture, the arrows, the sun in the corner. Then Ammi, folding clothes, said, "Afreen beti, tell me how a plant makes food." I said, "Sunlight... and the leaf... and then food." She waited. I couldn't remember what the leaf takes in, or what comes out. Hafsa giggled from the bed. I wanted to cry. It looked so familiar! Now I'm writing the steps on a card, one by one, and saying them out loud.

qa.q: What was Ammi doing when she asked Afreen to explain?
How did Afreen feel when she couldn't say the steps?
qa.a: Afreen felt upset and close to tears, because the page had looked so familiar that she was sure she knew it.

qa.q: Is Afreen's new plan a good one, and why?
qa.a: Yes; writing the steps on a card and saying them aloud makes Afreen recall them instead of just recognising the page.

qa.q: How might Ammi see Afreen's answer?
qa.a: Ammi waits patiently, likely noticing that Afreen knows the pictures but not the steps, and gives her the chance to find out before the test.

grounding: Illustrates a girl feeling ready because the photosynthesis page looks familiar, then failing to explain the steps when her mother asks.
